headline: Intel will pay Nvidia 1.5 billion dollars
text: On 10 January Nvidia and Intel settled their legal fight with a patent cross-licence: Intel will pay Nvidia 1.5 billion dollars in licence fees over six years. Nvidia will not make chipsets for Intel's newer processors; it is building up its Tegra processors for mobile devices.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, at Computex, Taipei, May 2010

headline: Tunisians chase out their ruler
text: On 17 December officials in the Tunisian town of Sidi Bouzid took away the cart of Mohamed Bouazizi, a 26-year-old street vendor, and refused to hear his complaint. His desperate protest, and his death on 4 January, set off demonstrations against poverty and corruption that spread across the country and reached the capital. On 14 January President Ben Ali, who had ruled for 23 years, fled to Saudi Arabia.
imageCaption: Tunisian revolution, 2011

headline: Another strong year: 62 million customers a day
text: McDonald's reported on 24 January that worldwide sales at existing restaurants rose 5.0% in 2010, positive in every region in every quarter. Revenue reached a record 24 billion dollars, earnings per share rose 11% to 4.58 dollars, and it returned 5.1 billion dollars to shareholders. More than 62 million customers visit its restaurants every day.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312511012490/dex991.htm (release of 24 January 2011, read 2026-10-03); yearly change from data/out/mcd.json
imageCaption: The Big Mac

headline: Altria grows earnings despite falling cigarette volumes
text: Altria reported on 27 January that its adjusted earnings per share rose 8.6% in 2010 to 1.90 dollars, helped by higher profits from cigarettes and smokeless tobacco, and announced a new 1 billion dollar share buyback. It expects 6 to 9% earnings growth in 2011.
imageCaption: Richmond, Virginia (photograph from 2021)

headline: China passes Japan as the world's second-largest economy
text: Figures released by Japan's government on 14 February put Japan's economy in 2010 at $5.47 trillion and China's at $5.88 trillion, measured in dollars at market exchange rates. That makes China the world's second-largest economy behind the United States, a place Japan had held for 42 years. Japan is still about ten times richer per person. A year ago China also overtook Germany as the world's biggest exporter.
imageCaption: Shoppers on a busy Beijing shopping street on the day figures confirmed that China had overtaken Japan as the second-largest economy, 14 February 2011
imageCredit: Photo by PETER PARKS/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Mubarak falls as protests sweep the Arab world
text: Eighteen days after protests began in Cairo's Tahrir Square on 25 January, Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak stepped down on 11 February and handed power to the army, ending 30 years in office. Tunisia's ruler had fled on 14 January after weeks of protest set off by a street vendor's self-immolation. Demonstrations are now spreading to Libya, Bahrain, Yemen and beyond. Hundreds of Egyptians were killed in the uprising.
imageCaption: Crowds in Tahrir Square, Cairo, 9 February 2011

headline: Libya's war pushes Brent above $110
text: Revolt against Muammar Gaddafi has shut much of Libya's oil output, after uprisings in Tunisia and Egypt. Brent ended February at $112 a barrel. US crude, priced at Cushing, Oklahoma, is about $15 cheaper, an unusually wide gap.
imageCaption: Libyan rebel fighters fire at government forces, 2011

headline: Nokia bets on Microsoft's Windows Phone
text: Days after a memo from Elop warned staff that Nokia was on a 'burning platform', Nokia announced on 11 February that it will use Microsoft's Windows Phone as its main smartphone software, instead of its own Symbian or Google's Android, and warned of substantial job cuts. Its share of the smartphone market fell from 38% to 28% in 2010. Its shares fell 12% that day.
imageCaption: Nokia chief executive Stephen Elop (left) and Microsoft's Steve Ballmer on stage in London as they announce that Nokia will switch to Windows Phone, 11 February 2011

headline: IBM's Watson wins at Jeopardy!
text: IBM's question-answering computer Watson beat the two most successful champions of the American quiz show Jeopardy!, Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter, and won the one-million-dollar first prize. IBM celebrates its 100th anniversary this year.
imageCaption: Watson's on-screen avatar and the IBM Power7 servers behind it, as staged for the Jeopardy! matches of February 2011

headline: Coca-Cola at 125: a billion more cases in a year
text: Coca-Cola, which celebrates 125 years in 2011, reported that its unit case volume grew 5% in 2010, adding more than a billion cases, and that it beat its long-term targets for volume and operating income. It now has more than 500 brands and closed the purchase of Coca-Cola Enterprises' North American business in October. Its '2020 Vision' plan, unveiled in 2009, sets the goals for the decade.
imageCaption: Muhtar Kent, Coca-Cola's chief executive, 2009

headline: Earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima
text: A magnitude 9 earthquake off north-east Japan on 11 March set off a tsunami that left tens of thousands dead or missing, and three reactors at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant were crippled, raising fears of meltdowns. The Nikkei fell more than 10% on 15 March to 8,605. The yen jumped, to about 79 per dollar on 17 March, and the G7 countries sold yen together on 18 March to weaken it.
imageCaption: A US Navy helicopter flies over Sendai after the earthquake and tsunami, March 2011

headline: Berkshire to buy Lubrizol for 9.7 billion dollars
text: On 14 March Berkshire agreed to buy the chemicals company Lubrizol for 135 dollars a share in cash, a 28% premium, in a deal valued at about 9.7 billion dollars including debt, one of the largest in Berkshire's history.
imageCaption: Motor oil being poured; Lubrizol makes the additives in such oils

headline: Cisco pays its first dividend
text: Cisco announced on March 18 its first cash dividend, 6 cents a share each quarter, payable April 20 to holders of record on March 31. At the current share price that is a yield of about 1.4%. The finance chief called it 'an important part of our commitment to bring value to shareholders.'
imageCaption: John Chambers, Cisco's chairman and chief executive, at the World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2010

headline: Prince William marries Catherine Middleton
text: Prince William married Catherine Middleton at Westminster Abbey on 29 April. About a million people lined the route in London, and tens of millions watched around the world, 72 million of them on live streams on YouTube.
imageCaption: Prince William and Catherine on their wedding day, 29 April 2011

headline: Hackers break into the PlayStation Network
text: Sony learned on 19 April of an intrusion into its PlayStation Network and shut the service down. Personal details from about 77 million accounts were compromised, one of the largest data breaches so far.
imageCaption: Visitors try PlayStation Network games at the Sony booth, E3, Los Angeles, June 2011

headline: Glencore goes public in London's largest premium listing
text: Glencore, the Baar-based trader founded in 1974 as Marc Rich + Co and bought out by its managers in 1994, priced its IPO at 530p a share on 19 May, raising about $10bn and valuing itself at $59.2bn, the largest premium listing ever in London. It handles an estimated 60% of the world's traded zinc and half of its traded copper, plus oil, coal and grain, and owns mines and a third of Xstrata, much of whose output it markets. Shares began trading in London on 24 May and in Hong Kong a day later; managers keep about 83% of the company.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/glencore-international-plc-ipo-successfully-priced/2640217; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glencore (history and 2010 market shares, citing the Guardian 19 May 2011); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Rich (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Glencore's headquarters in Baar, Switzerland

headline: Nokia scraps its forecasts
text: On 31 May Nokia said second-quarter phone sales will be substantially below its forecast and its margin below the 6-9% range, withdrew its full-year guidance and said it is taking immediate action. Its shares fell 14%.
imageCaption: Stephen Elop, 2008

headline: Citigroup completes a 1-for-10 reverse split
text: Citigroup combined every ten of its shares into one, effective after trading on 6 May; the shares trade on a split-adjusted basis from 9 May. A shareholder's stake is unchanged: ten times fewer shares, each worth ten times more. Citigroup plans to reinstate a quarterly dividend of 1 cent a share now that the split is done. It earned $10.6 billion in 2010.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000119312511131957/dex991.htm (Citigroup press release, 9 May 2011; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000114420411016019/v215370_ex99-1.htm (21 March 2011; read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Open outcry, 2001

headline: Microsoft buys Skype
text: On 10 May Microsoft agreed to buy Skype, the internet telephone service, for about 8.5 billion dollars.
imageCaption: A Skype balloon at the SXSW festival in Austin, March 2012

headline: eBay buys GSI Commerce
text: eBay acquired GSI Commerce, which runs online shops for large retailers, for $2.4 billion.
imageCaption: An eBay Enterprise centre in Georgia, the former GSI Commerce

headline: Supreme Court throws out the giant discrimination suit
text: On 20 June the US Supreme Court ruled that the women suing Wal-Mart for sex discrimination cannot proceed as a single class of about 1.5 million, because their claims do not share a common question. All nine justices agreed the class was improper.
imageCaption: Betty Dukes, the Wal-Mart employee who led the discrimination suit, at a meeting in Congress

headline: Cisco cuts 6,500 jobs and closes Flip
text: On July 18 Cisco said it will cut about 6,500 jobs, around 9% of its regular workforce, as part of $1 billion of annual cost savings after disappointing profits. With the sale of a set-top box plant in Mexico and the closure of the Flip video camera business, about 12,000 jobs go in all. Competitors such as Juniper, HP and Huawei are pressing Cisco in its core markets.
imageCaption: A Flip Mino HD pocket video camera

headline: Andrew Gould retires; Paal Kibsgaard takes over
text: On 21 July Schlumberger said Andrew Gould would retire as chief executive on 1 August and stay chairman until April 2012. He will be succeeded by Paal Kibsgaard, the chief operating officer, who has worked for the company for more than 14 years in the Middle East, Europe and the United States.
imageCaption: Schlumberger's research centre in Cambridge, later named after Andrew Gould

headline: America loses its AAA rating and shares plunge
text: Late on 5 August Standard and Poor's cut the United States' credit rating from AAA to AA+, the first time the country has lost the agency's top rating, after a bitter fight in Congress over the debt ceiling. On Monday 8 August the S&P 500 fell 6.7% to 1,119.46, as fears grew that Europe's debt crisis would spread to Italy and Spain and that America would fall back into recession. European regulators banned short selling of bank shares from 11 August, and the S&P 500 ended August down 6%. Investors fled into Treasury bonds and gold, which averaged a record 1,759 dollars in August, 12 percent more than in July. In Germany the DAX fell from 7,376 at the end of June to around 5,250 in early September, with car makers hit hardest; Daimler's shares lost 26% in August.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_2011_stock_markets_fall (read 2026-10-03); data/reference/sp500.json; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_United_States_debt-ceiling_crisis (read 2026-10-03); https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20110809a.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20101103a.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GS10 (read 2026-10-03); data/out/gold.json (read 2026-10-03); BMW Group Annual Report 2011, capital market section (DAX -30% July to September), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2011.pdf (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jason Blatt of Knight Capital reacts on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on the first trading day after America lost its AAA rating, 8 August 2011
imageCredit: Photo by STAN HONDA/AFP via Getty Images

headline: The strong franc makes shopping across the border cheap
text: From May 2010 to early August 2011 the Swiss franc rose by more than 30 per cent against the euro, as investors fled the euro debt crisis. For Swiss families, holidays abroad and the shops in Germany, France and Italy have become much cheaper, while the export industry at home suffers. Shoppers can also reclaim German VAT.
imageCaption: Konstanz, the German town on the Swiss border where many Swiss go shopping

headline: The Fed promises: money stays free for two more years
text: Central banks rarely say what they will do far ahead. On 9 August the Fed did: it expects to keep its interest rate at 'exceptionally low levels', between 0 and 0.25 percent, 'at least through mid-2013'. Money has now been free for almost three years. The numbers: the Fed's rate 0.1 percent. Inflation 3.6 percent. Unemployment 9.0 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to August 2011
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Apple becomes the world's most valuable company
text: In August Apple passed ExxonMobil as the most valuable listed company in the world. It had passed Microsoft in May 2010, for the first time since 1989.
imageCaption: Apple's glass-cube store on Fifth Avenue, New York, December 2010

headline: Strong first results, falling markets
text: In its first results as a listed company on 25 August, Glencore reported first-half adjusted EBITDA of $3.85bn, up 47%, declared a maiden dividend of 5 US cents and said its credit ratings had been upgraded. It warned of 'renewed sovereign debt concerns' after a month in which the United States lost its AAA rating and stock markets slumped. The day before it offered to buy out the minority in its Australian nickel miner Minara.
imageCaption: Glencore's Kidd copper and zinc mine near Timmins, Ontario

headline: Jobs resigns; Tim Cook is chief executive
text: On 24 August Steve Jobs resigned as Apple's chief executive, writing to the board that he could no longer meet his duties and expectations. Tim Cook succeeds him.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs on stage in 2011, his last year as Apple's chief executive

headline: Tillerson and Putin's oil chief sign an Arctic deal
text: In August, with Vladimir Putin attending in Sochi, Rex Tillerson and Rosneft's Igor Sechin signed an agreement for ExxonMobil and Russia's state oil company to drill the East-Prinovozemelsky field in the Arctic Ocean, a partnership talked of as worth up to 300 billion dollars.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 29 April 2022 (Sakhalin-1 charge), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408822000023/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Igor Sechin, Rosneft's chief

headline: Euro crisis and slowing China crush miners
text: Fears that the euro debt crisis will spread to Italy and Spain, after the United States lost its AAA rating in August, have driven investors out of cyclical shares. Copper averaged $8,300 a tonne in September, down from $9,650 in July, and fell further late in the month. Mining shares were among the worst performers.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_2011_stock_markets_fall; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The bull and bear statues outside the Frankfurt stock exchange

headline: A rogue trader costs UBS $2.3 billion; Grübel resigns
text: On 15 September UBS said unauthorised trading by a trader in London, Kweku Adoboli, had caused a loss estimated at $2 billion, later put at $2.3 billion; the shares fell 10.8% that day. On 24 September chief executive Oswald Grübel resigned; Sergio Ermotti takes over on an interim basis. Earlier in the month, on 6 September, the Swiss National Bank set a minimum exchange rate of 1.20 francs per euro, and the franc fell about 11% against the dollar in September.
imageCaption: Police lead Kweku Adoboli, the trader blamed for the loss, from a London court, September 2011

headline: The National Bank caps the franc at 1.20 per euro
text: On 6 September the Swiss National Bank set a minimum rate of 1.20 francs per euro, saying the strong franc threatens the economy and that it will buy foreign currency in unlimited quantities. The franc fell about 11% against the dollar in September. Nestlé's share was almost unchanged in francs. Novartis shares rose about 8% in francs.
imageCaption: Philipp Hildebrand, chairman of the Swiss National Bank, at the St. Gallen Symposium

headline: First 787 delivered to ANA
text: Boeing handed over the first 787 Dreamliner to All Nippon Airways on 25-26 September, three years later than the 2008 date planned at launch.
imageCaption: An All Nippon Airways Boeing 787 Dreamliner

headline: Siemens quits nuclear power
text: Siemens, which built all 17 of Germany's nuclear power plants, said it will leave the nuclear business after the Fukushima disaster and Germany's decision to phase out nuclear power. Chief executive Löscher backs the country's switch to renewable energy.
imageCaption: Peter Löscher, Siemens' chief executive (photograph from 2012)

headline: Euro summit: banks to take half off Greek debt
text: Three euro countries now live on rescue loans: Greece since May 2010, Ireland since November 2010 and Portugal since May, with 78 billion euros. In the night of 26 to 27 October euro leaders agreed that private banks will write off 50 percent of their Greek bonds, that Europe's banks must raise more capital, and that the rescue fund's firepower is to be raised to about one trillion euros. On 31 October the Greek prime minister, George Papandreou, surprised his partners by announcing a referendum on the deal. The S&P 500, which on 4 October stood about 21% below its May peak, rose 11% in October to 1,253.30, its best month since 1991.
imageCaption: Angela Merkel and Nicolas Sarkozy at the euro summit in Brussels that agreed a 50 percent cut in Greek debt, October 2011

headline: Citigroup's profit rises to $3.8 billion
text: Citigroup reported third-quarter net income of $3.8 billion, up from $2.2 billion a year earlier, although $1.9 billion of it came from an accounting gain on the fall in the value of its own debt. Credit losses fell 41%. After two months of steep losses, bank shares recovered, and Citigroup's rose 23% in October.
imageCaption: A Citibank branch in Guangzhou, China

headline: Steve Jobs dies
text: Steve Jobs died at his home in Palo Alto on 5 October, aged 56, after a relapse of the pancreatic tumour first diagnosed in 2003. He co-founded Apple, had stepped down as chief executive six weeks earlier, and was behind the Macintosh, the iPod, the iPhone and the iPad.
imageCaption: Tribute to Steve Jobs outside an Apple Store, Palo Alto, October 2011

headline: Amazon sells the Kindle Fire at $199 and profits drop
text: On October 25 Amazon reported third-quarter sales of $10.88 billion, up 44%, but net income fell 73% to $63 million. It is launching the Kindle Fire tablet at $199 and other Kindles from $79.
imageCaption: The first Amazon Kindle Fire tablet

headline: Italy's borrowing costs pass 7 percent; Berlusconi and Papandreou go
text: On 9 November the interest rate on Italy's ten-year bonds rose above 7 percent, to as much as 7.45 percent, a level many economists see as unbearable; Italy's debt equals 120 percent of its economic output, and it is seen as too big to rescue with the funds available. Silvio Berlusconi resigned as prime minister on 12 November, and the economist Mario Monti was sworn in on 16 November at the head of a government of unelected experts. In Greece, George Papandreou dropped his referendum plan and resigned on 10 November; Lucas Papademos now leads a national unity government.
imageCaption: Silvio Berlusconi, 2010

headline: Record year for Disney
text: On 10 November Disney reported record revenue and profit for its business year to October: earnings per share rose 24% to 2.52 dollars and net income 21% to 4.8 billion dollars. Chief executive Bob Iger called it a great year financially and strategically.
imageCaption: The Mickey Mouse Ferris wheel at Disney California Adventure

headline: 2011 in review: a year of turmoil ends exactly flat
text: The S&P 500 ended 2011 at 1,257.60, almost exactly where it began (1,257.64), after falling about 21% between May and October. The Dow gained 5.5%. America's downgrade and Europe's debt crisis made it one of the most volatile years in memory.
imageCaption: American shares (S&P 500) at the end of each month of 2011: down 0 percent in the year
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC, month-end closes)
